questions.stem: One of the mechanisms for intestinal sugar absorption is mediated by the Na+-K+ ATPase pump. Which of the following sugars require sodium for absorption?GlucoseSucroseGalactoseFructoseMaltoseSelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
1, & 3 are correct

Statements:  1 and 3. Glucose and Galactose

  • Galactose and Glucose are transported into mucosal cells by an active, energy-requiring process that requires a concurrent uptake of sodium ions and this transport protein is SGLT-1 (Sodium-dependent Glucose Tramantransport).

Sodium-dependent transporter of glucose

  • SGLT-1 → Small intestine and Kidneys → for Glucose and Galactose
  • SGLT-2 → Kidneys → only for Glucose




Lippincott’s Illustrated Reviews 7th Edition Page No. 87

questions.stem: GLUTs and SGLTs are two types of sugar transporter present in the intestine and kidneys. Which of the following transporters is defective in renal glycosuria?
questions.solutionHtml:
SGLT- 2
  • In this disease, blood glucose is normal, but still Glucose appears in the urine.
  • It is due to a defect/mutation in SGLT-2, which is major glucose transporter (90% glucose reabsorption) present in kidneys for the reabsorption and transport of Glucose (see fig below).



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 187

questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct statement regarding sugar transport in humans?

options.label: A
options.text: GLUT-2 responsible for glucose and fructose absorption

options.label: B
options.text: Glucose is absorbed independent of Sodium

questions.solutionHtml:
SGLT-2 is specific for glucose
  • SGLT-2 is major glucose transporter (90% glucose reabsorption) present in kidneys (in renal tubules.
  • Deficiency of SGLT-2 leads to renal glycosuria with glucose excretion in urine.


Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 187

questions.stem: One manner in which type 2 diabetes occurs is via a reduction in the release of insulin from the pancreas. The release of insulin from the β-cells of the pancreas requires which of the following GLUT transporters?
questions.solutionHtml:
GLUT-2

Option: B. GLUT-2

  • Is present in the pancreas, intestine, and liver
  • It is active in the fed state.
  • It acts as a glucose sensor in blood and allows glucose uptake in the pancreas postprandially for stimulation and release of insulin from beta cells of the pancreas (see fig below).




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 187

questions.stem: A variety of passive glucose transporters (GLUTs) are involved in glucose transport to various tissues and organs under different conditions. After overnight fasting, GLUTs are reduced in:
questions.solutionHtml:
Adipose tissues
  • Synthesis of GLUT-4 channels is induced in response to insulin secretion after a carbohydrate-rich. They transport glucose to
    • Skeletal muscles
    • Cardiac muscles
    • Adipose tissues
  • Once the blood glucose is transported, their number also gets So, after an overnight fast (low blood glucose), these GLUTs will be reduced in skeletal muscles, cardiac muscles & adipose tissues due to low insulin.



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 187-188

questions.stem: A child of 5 years of age was given high fructose corn syrup. The child develops abdominal pain and diarrhea. Consultation with the physician and the history of the patient reveals the occurrence of dietary fructose intolerance in the child. Deficiency of one of the following is implicated in the pathophysiology of the disorder?
questions.solutionHtml:
GLUT-5

GLUT-5 is the exclusive fructose transporter. It is expressed in the apical borders of enterocytes in the small intestine. It brings about the facilitated transport of fructose from the lumen of the small intestine to inside the enterocytes in favor of the fructose concentration gradient.


Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 7th Edition, Page No. 87

questions.stem: Arrange the following in sequence occurring in a fed state:InsulinGLUT-2Uptake of glucose by skeletal musclesGLUT-4Select the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
2→1→4→3

Option: C.  2→1→4→3

During Fed state:

  • GLUT-2 ⇒ Insulin ⇒ GLUT- 4 ⇒ Uptake of glucose by skeletal muscles
  • After the reduction of blood glucose, GLUT-2 expression is decreased causing low insulin and low GLUT-4 expression.



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 188

questions.stem: Which of the following DOES NOT depend on insulin for glucose uptake?
questions.solutionHtml:
Brain
  • In the brain, glucose uptake is mediated by GLUT-1 & GLUT-3 which are involved in basal glucose uptake in the fed and fasting state (mainly).
  • These GLUTs are active irrespective of the presence or absence of insulin. So, there is no relation between insulin and these GLUTs or we can say that GLUT-1 and 3 are not dependent on insulin.
  • So, Brain does not depend on insulin for glucose uptake.

.




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 187-188

questions.stem: The facilitative transporter GLUT-2 is responsible for the activation of the insulin-induced GLUT-4 transporter and the transport of blood glucose to peripheral tissues. Mutation in GLUT-2 causes which of the following disease?
questions.solutionHtml:
Fanconi-Bickel syndrome
  • The autosomal recessive condition caused due to allelic variants of GLUT-2 arose due to mutations.

C/F

  • Resembles type I GSD (von Gierke’s disease) - Glycogen deposited in the liver and kidney
  • Fasting hypoglycemia but postprandial hyperglycemia
  • Patients are usually dwarf, with rickets, aminoaciduria, phosphaturia, glucosuria, Proximal tubulopathy, and hypercalciuria



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 174

questions.stem: The method of transport of glucose in the intestine is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Secondary active transport
  • The method of transport of glucose in the intestine is called Secondary active transport.
  • Both glucose and Na+ enter inside the cell (in the same direction) i.e. Symport.
  • No energy is used when glucose and Na+ enter the cell.
  • Energy is used indirectly for glucose transport via Na+- K+ ATPase pump.
  • A sodium-glucose symporter carries 2Na+ for each glucose
  • In the intestine on the luminal surface, there is SGLT-1 (secondary active transport) while on the basal surface is GLUT-2 (facilitative transport)




Textbook of Medical Biochemistry by Dinesh Puri 3rd Edition Page No. 139-141

questions.stem: True Statement regarding the intestinal brush border membrane is:

options.label: A
options.text: Amylase is only found in the brush border

options.label: B
options.text: Disaccharides can cross the brush border

options.label: C
options.text: Insulin is required for the uptake of glucose

options.label: D
options.text: Fructose requires a sodium-independent monosaccharide transporter

questions.answerText: Fructose requires a sodium-independent monosaccharide transporter
questions.solutionHtml:
Fructose requires a sodium-independent monosaccharide transporter
  • Fructose absorption is dependent on GLUT-5 which is a sodium-independent transporter
  • This transporter is mainly present in the liver and testis.



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 187
